title: Reflex Budget
one_liner: Slide network latency and watch a cloud-controlled robot lose balance where an onboard brain stays upright.
speaker: Brett Adcock
context: Brett explains that all of Helix runs onboard because the best 5G gives about 20–30 ms per leg, roughly 50 ms round trip, which caps control at about 20Hz before any inference even starts.
demo: Two side-by-side stick-figure humanoids balance on one foot while carrying a tray, and random shoves hit both. One runs an onboard control loop; the other routes through a 'cloud' with adjustable per-leg latency and inference time. A live readout shows the effective control rate in Hz. As latency grows, the cloud robot wobbles and falls, and a counter tracks falls per minute.
data_plan: The latency anchors are episode figures. The balance physics is a simplified simulation, clearly labeled.
risks: The pendulum physics is a toy. Fall thresholds should be labeled illustrative, not real robot data.
